text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Paul Martin strikes Canada Pension Plan deal; Ottawa gives ground to Ontario in unemployment insurance premiums to get province's support.
- Defection puts China on spot; North Korean creates no-win situation.
- 'Fiscal discipline' a priority, Prime Minister says; Prebudget talk focuses on achievements.
- Metro Toronto Council votes for unified city; Council shifts from stance championing local government.
- Hostility erupts at Guy Paul Morin inquiry; Morin's former defence counsel blamed for his wrongful conviction.
- Postwar marriages good as gold; As boomers approach 50, they are holding parties to celebrate their mothers' and fathers' half century together.
- Morrison Petroleums Ltd finds friendly suitor; Northstar Energy Corp to take over oil firm days after Canadian 88 Energy Corp drops hostile bid.
- Dow cracks 7,000 for first time; Bonds help stocks rewrite record books.
- Magna International Inc bids for German firm; Auto parts giant aims to be a force in seat making in Europe.
- Wascana Energy Inc shares surge on hope for fight against Talisman Energy Inc bid; Target may try to push for more money.

- Morrison Petroleum Ltd finds white knight; Northstar Energy Corp rides to the rescue with a friendly C$650-million share-swap offer, less than a week after Canadian 88 abruptly killed its hostile takeover bid.
